references.text: The mountain burned with fire all the way to heaven, with darkness, clouds and mist - describing the same event at Sinai with fire and smoke.
The Lord spoke from the fire, cloud and darkness on the mountain - a parallel description of the theophany at Sinai.
The Lord came from Sinai and shone forth - a reference to God's revelation at Mount Sinai.
The mountains quaked before the Lord's presence, before Sinai, before the Lord, the God of Israel - a poetic reference to the earthquake at Sinai.
Smoke rose from his nostrils, devouring fire from his mouth - a poetic image of God's presence with fire and smoke.
The earth shook, the heavens dripped at God's presence, Sinai quaked before God, the presence of the God of Israel - a direct reference to the earthquake at Sinai.
He looks on the earth, and it trembles; he touches the mountains, and they smoke - describing God's power to make mountains smoke.
Bow your heavens, Lord, and come down; touch the mountains so that they smoke - a prayer with an image of God's presence causing mountains to smoke.
The doorposts shook at the voice of those who shouted, and the house was filled with smoke - a theophany with shaking and smoke.
Describes the Sinai event with burning fire, darkness, storm, trumpet sound and a voice - a New Testament reference to the theophany at Sinai.
The temple was filled with smoke from God's glory and his power - smoke as a sign of God's presence, like the Sinai event.
Exodus 24:17 completes the picture of God's presence by describing how the fire looked to the Israelites.
Exodus 24:16 provides context for the cloud and glory that followed the initial smoke in chapter 19.
